task_summary: Define the interface contract for the 'Availability Bitmask Cache Layer' component (availability_bitmask_cache). This component builds and maintains Redis-cached bitmasks from PostgreSQL availability_blocks data, exposing checkAvailability(unitId, startDate, endDate) → boolean and invalidateCache(unitId). It uses hash-sharded Redis keys (avail:{hash(unit_id) % 64}:{unit_id}) with a 365-day sliding window. The contract must specify types, error handling, serialization, and naming conventions for a Deno/TypeScript + Redis + PostgreSQL stack.

findings.finding: A 365-day availability window maps naturally to a 365-bit bitmask (46 bytes). Redis BITFIELD and GETRANGE commands can operate on binary strings directly, enabling O(1) sub-range checks via bitwise AND against a pre-computed range mask. The anchor date (day 0) must be explicitly stored or derived deterministically (e.g., today's UTC date or a fixed epoch) so that bit positions are unambiguous. A rolling-window approach where day 0 = today requires daily rotation/rebuild, whereas a fixed-epoch approach (day 0 = a known date) avoids rotation but needs offset math.
findings.source: Redis documentation on BITFIELD/SETBIT/GETBIT; industry patterns from booking/calendar systems (Airbnb engineering blog, Booking.com tech talks)
findings.relevance: Core data structure choice — the interface must expose or abstract the anchor-date concept and define how bit positions map to calendar dates.

findings.topic: Redis key design and hash-slot sharding
findings.finding: The key format avail:{hash(unit_id) % 64}:{unit_id} distributes keys across 64 logical shards. This is a well-established pattern for Redis Cluster compatibility — using hash tags {shard} ensures all keys for a shard land on the same cluster node. However, since unit_id is a UUID (128-bit), the hash function must be deterministic and consistent across services. A common approach: use a fast non-cryptographic hash (e.g., CRC32 or FNV-1a) of the UUID string, mod 64. The interface contract should specify the exact hash algorithm to prevent cross-service inconsistencies.
findings.source: Redis Cluster specification (hash slots); distributed caching best practices
findings.relevance: The key format is part of the public contract since other components or debugging tools may need to derive keys. The hash algorithm must be specified precisely.

findings.topic: TypeScript type design for bitmask cache interfaces
findings.finding: Best practice is to use branded/opaque types for domain identifiers (UnitId as a branded string type) to prevent accidental misuse. Date parameters should be typed as ISO 8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD) not full timestamps, since availability is day-granularity. A dedicated DateString branded type prevents passing datetime strings. Return types should use discriminated unions for success/error cases rather than throwing exceptions, especially at module boundaries. The Result<T, E> pattern (inspired by Rust) is idiomatic in modern TypeScript for composable error handling.
findings.source: TypeScript handbook (branded types); fp-ts and neverthrow libraries; Deno standard library patterns
findings.relevance: Directly applicable — the interface contract needs precise type definitions that prevent misuse and encode domain constraints at the type level.

findings.topic: Cache invalidation patterns — lazy rebuild vs eager rebuild
findings.finding: Lazy invalidation (delete key, rebuild on next read) is simpler and preferred when read frequency is moderate. However, it introduces a cache-miss latency spike (cold read penalty). For high-traffic units, a hybrid approach — invalidate + async pre-warm — avoids thundering herd. The interface should expose invalidateCache as fire-and-forget (void return) but internally should handle the case where multiple concurrent reads trigger simultaneous rebuilds. A common pitfall: not using a distributed lock or single-flight pattern, causing N concurrent cache-miss queries to PostgreSQL for the same unit_id.
findings.source: Cache-aside pattern (Microsoft architecture docs); singleflight pattern (Go stdlib, adaptable to TS); Redis SETNX for distributed locks
findings.relevance: The invalidateCache contract needs to document behavior under concurrent access. The checkAvailability contract needs to document cache-miss behavior and latency characteristics.

findings.topic: Error handling conventions at cache layer boundaries
findings.finding: Cache layers should degrade gracefully: if Redis is unavailable, fall back to direct PostgreSQL query. The interface should define explicit error types: CacheMiss (normal, triggers rebuild), CacheUnavailable (Redis down, fallback), DataNotFound (unit doesn't exist in PostgreSQL), InvalidDateRange (start > end, range exceeds 365 days, dates in the past). Throwing generic errors across module boundaries makes contract testing fragile. Instead, define a closed set of error codes/types as part of the contract.
findings.source: Circuit breaker pattern (Hystrix/Resilience4j concepts); Netflix reliability engineering practices
findings.relevance: Critical for the interface contract — callers need to know exactly what error states are possible and how to handle them.

findings.finding: A 365-day bitmask cached with a fixed TTL (e.g., 24h) balances freshness vs load. However, the TTL should be configurable and documented in the interface. A common pitfall: not accounting for the sliding window — if the bitmask is anchored to a fixed date, after 24h the first bit(s) may represent past dates. Best practice: anchor to the start of the current UTC day, set TTL to expire at end of day (or use a 24h TTL), and always validate that requested dates fall within the bitmask's valid range. The contract should specify what happens when querying dates outside the 365-day window.
findings.source: Calendar/booking system engineering practices; Redis TTL documentation
findings.relevance: The interface must document the valid query range and behavior for out-of-range date requests.

findings.topic: Serialization format for bitmask storage in Redis
findings.finding: Two main approaches: (1) Store as a raw binary string using Redis SETBIT/GETBIT — most space-efficient (46 bytes for 365 bits) and allows server-side bit operations. (2) Store as a base64-encoded string — portable and debuggable but requires client-side bit manipulation. For this use case, raw binary (Redis bit string) is preferred since Redis BITCOUNT and BITFIELD can do range checks server-side. The interface contract should specify the internal format even though callers don't directly interact with it, for debugging and cross-service consistency.
findings.source: Redis bit operations documentation; binary protocol best practices
findings.relevance: Internal implementation detail but should be documented in the contract for operational clarity and future interoperability.

findings.finding: Deno 2.x supports npm packages natively, so the 'ioredis' or 'redis' npm packages work. Alternatively, deno-redis (r/redis on deno.land/x) is a native Deno Redis client. For PostgreSQL, deno-postgres (deno.land/x/postgres) is the standard. The interface should be client-agnostic — depend on abstractions (a RedisClient interface and a PgClient interface) not concrete implementations, enabling easy mocking in tests per the project's testing requirements.
findings.source: Deno 2.x documentation; deno.land/x registry; project operating procedures (mock DB/Redis requirement)
findings.relevance: The contract should define dependency injection interfaces for Redis and PostgreSQL clients to support testability requirements.

findings.finding: The parent context mentions a bulk endpoint (GET /availability/bulk?unit_ids=&start=&end=). The cache layer should expose a bulk method (checkBulkAvailability) that uses Redis MGET or pipeline to fetch multiple bitmasks in a single round trip. A common pitfall: not batching Redis calls for bulk operations, resulting in N sequential round trips. The interface should define this bulk method even if initially implemented as a loop, to prevent callers from implementing their own batching logic.
findings.source: Redis pipelining documentation; bulk operation patterns in caching layers
findings.relevance: The parent REST API has a bulk endpoint — the cache layer interface needs a corresponding bulk method for efficiency.

findings.topic: Date boundary edge cases in bitmask operations
findings.finding: Frequently missed edge cases: (1) Timezone issues — availability must be strictly UTC day-aligned; the contract must enforce this. (2) Off-by-one errors in date range inclusion — is the range [start, end] inclusive on both ends? Must be specified. (3) Leap years — 365-bit bitmask may need to be 366 bits in leap years, or the system can always allocate 366 bits. (4) Querying a single day (start == end). (5) The bitmask anchor date rolling over at midnight UTC — concurrent requests during rollover may see stale data. (6) What 'available' means for today's date (partially elapsed day).
findings.source: Booking system engineering post-mortems; date/time handling best practices (W3C, ISO 8601)
findings.relevance: These edge cases must be explicitly addressed in the interface contract to prevent bugs in consuming services.

recommended_approach:
Define the interface contract using the following structure:

1. **Branded Types**: Define `UnitId` (branded UUID string), `DateString` (branded YYYY-MM-DD ISO 8601 string), and `ShardKey` (branded number 0-63) to enforce domain constraints at the type level.

2. **Result Type**: Use a discriminated union `Result<T, AvailabilityError>` where `AvailabilityError` is a union of `InvalidDateRange | UnitNotFound | CacheUnavailable | InternalError`, each with an error code and message.

3. **Core Interface** (`AvailabilityBitmaskCache`):
   - `checkAvailability(unitId: UnitId, startDate: DateString, endDate: DateString): Promise<Result<boolean, AvailabilityError>>` — inclusive date range [start, end], max 365 days, must be today or future.
   - `checkBulkAvailability(unitIds: UnitId[], startDate: DateString, endDate: DateString): Promise<Result<Map<UnitId, boolean>, AvailabilityError>>` — batched Redis pipeline for bulk lookups.
   - `invalidateCache(unitId: UnitId): Promise<Result<void, AvailabilityError>>` — deletes the cached bitmask; next read triggers lazy rebuild.

4. **Dependency Injection Interfaces**: Define `RedisClient` and `PgClient` abstractions that the cache layer depends on, enabling mock injection for tests.

5. **Configuration Type**: Define `CacheConfig` with `ttlSeconds`, `shardCount` (default 64), `windowDays` (default 366 to handle leap years), `hashAlgorithm` (CRC32), `keyPrefix` ('avail').

6. **Internal Contracts** (documented but not exposed): Bitmask is a raw Redis bit string, 366 bits, anchored to today's UTC date (bit 0 = today, bit 365 = today + 365 days). 1 = available, 0 = blocked. Key format: `avail:{CRC32(unit_id) % 64}:{unit_id}`.

7. **Edge Case Handling**: Date range is inclusive on both ends. Querying past dates returns InvalidDateRange error. Single-day queries (start == end) are supported. Singleflight pattern prevents thundering herd on cache miss. Redis unavailability triggers PostgreSQL fallback (logged as warning).

8. **Contract Tests**: Define request/response shape tests for each method, including error cases. Mock Redis and PostgreSQL per project standards.
alternatives_considered: Fixed-epoch anchor (e.g., 2024-01-01) vs rolling-window anchor (today's UTC date): Fixed epoch avoids daily rebuild but wastes bits on past dates and requires larger bitmasks over time. Rolling window (anchor = today) keeps bitmask compact at 366 bits but requires daily expiration/rebuild. Recommend: rolling window anchored to today's UTC date with TTL expiring at end of UTC day.

Raw Redis bit string vs base64-encoded string vs JSON array of 0/1: Raw bit string is most efficient and allows server-side BITCOUNT/BITFIELD operations. Base64 is portable but requires client-side decoding. JSON array is wasteful (365+ bytes vs 46). Recommend: raw Redis bit string with SETBIT/GETBIT.

Result<T, E> discriminated union vs thrown exceptions for error handling: Result type is more explicit, testable, and composable. Exceptions are simpler but leak across module boundaries unpredictably. Recommend: Result<T, E> pattern at the interface boundary, with specific error type union.

Single checkAvailability method vs separate getCachedBitmask + checkRange: Exposing the raw bitmask enables callers to do multiple range checks without repeated cache lookups. However, it leaks implementation details. Recommend: keep checkAvailability as the primary interface but add an optional getBitmask for advanced/bulk use cases.

Eager cache rebuild on invalidation vs lazy rebuild on next read: Eager avoids cold-read latency but adds write-path complexity and may rebuild unnecessarily. Lazy is simpler and sufficient for moderate traffic. Recommend: lazy rebuild with singleflight protection against thundering herd.

CRC32 vs FNV-1a vs simple modulo of UUID segments for hash sharding: All are acceptable. CRC32 is widely available and well-distributed. Recommend: CRC32 of the UUID string representation, mod 64, for determinism and broad language support.
risks: Thundering herd on cache miss: Multiple concurrent reads for the same unit_id during cache rebuild can overwhelm PostgreSQL. Mitigate with singleflight/mutex pattern.

Bitmask anchor date rollover at UTC midnight: Requests spanning the rollover moment may read a stale bitmask anchored to yesterday. Mitigate by checking anchor date validity before returning cached results.

Hash algorithm inconsistency across services: If any other service needs to compute the Redis key, using a different hash function or different string representation of UUID will produce wrong keys. Mitigate by documenting exact algorithm (CRC32 of lowercase UUID string with hyphens) in the contract.
Leap year handling: A 365-bit bitmask is insufficient for years spanning Feb 29. Mitigate by always using 366 bits.

Redis key collision or stale data: If TTL is set incorrectly or invalidation fails silently, stale availability data could cause double bookings. Mitigate by making invalidation return success/failure and logging all failures.
Off-by-one in date-to-bit-position mapping: Inclusive vs exclusive range boundaries are a classic source of booking bugs. Mitigate by explicit contract specification and thorough edge-case tests.

PostgreSQL fallback under Redis outage may not handle load: If Redis goes down and all traffic falls through to PostgreSQL, the database may be overwhelmed. Mitigate by documenting this risk and recommending rate limiting or circuit breaking in the implementation.
compliance_notes: All dates must be ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD), UTC, per project standards.
UUIDs for all entity identifiers (unit_id) per project standards.
Type annotations required on all public functions per project standards.
All functions must have at least one test; tests must be runnable without external services (mock Redis/PostgreSQL) per project standards.
Integration boundaries must have contract tests validating request/response shapes per project standards.
Files must stay under 300 lines per project standards — interface definition, types, implementation, and tests should be separate files.
Prefer Deno stdlib over third-party libraries where possible per project standards.
Service must be independently deployable under services/availability_bitmask_cache/ per project standards.
